editor.stage.focusTitle: Frame Selected: the selected part (whole model if none) · numpad . / F · double-tap a part

editor.origin.heading: Origin
editor.origin.affectTitle: Options › Transform › Affect Only Origins: the move tool and G move only the origin, the part stays put · snaps to vertices, edge midpoints, face centres, box corners/centre and the grid · hold Alt for free movement
editor.origin.affectOnHint: Affect Only Origins: drag the arrows or press G to move the origin (rotating / scaling origins is not supported)
editor.origin.noRotate: Rotating / scaling origins is not supported — turn off Affect Only Origins
editor.origin.localSub: Origin, cm · local: part axes, from the original GLB origin
editor.origin.worldSub: Origin, cm · global: scene axes (X right, Y up, Z front)
editor.cursor.placeTitle: Place 3D Cursor: tap / click a surface (desktop: Shift+right-click anywhere) · Shift+C puts it back at the world origin
editor.cursor.hint: Tap a surface to place the 3D cursor
editor.modal.keys: [LMB / Enter] Confirm · [RMB / Esc] Cancel · [X] [Y] [Z] Axis (twice: local) · [Ctrl] Snap {snap} · [Shift] Precision · [0-9 . -] Type a value
editor.keys.tip: Blender keys: G / R / S move · rotate · scale, then X / Y / Z for an axis, type a value, click / Enter to confirm, right-click / Esc to cancel · Shift+D duplicate · X / Delete delete · A select the whole object · Alt+A deselect · Alt+G / R / S clear the whole-object location / rotation / scale · N sidebar · numpad . / F frame selected · Home frame all · Shift+right-click 3D cursor · Shift+C reset cursor · middle-drag orbit, Shift+middle-drag pan, wheel zoom
editor.place.scopeObjectTitle: Clicks select the whole object (Object mode on the root) · A
editor.place.heading: Whole object · Object mode
editor.place.scaleWarn: Scaling the whole object changes its real-world size (the furniture would no longer be its real size). Unlock only if you mean it.
editor.place.scaleBlocked: Scale is locked: it changes the real-world size. Unlock it with the lock icon in the sidebar.
editor.place.floorSnapTitle: While moving / rotating the whole object with snapping on, a base within 3 cm of the floor lands exactly on it (Ctrl toggles snapping)
editor.place.cameraNote: The mock-up camera stays fixed: moving the whole object moves it within the mock-up view (the camera-match solve works in the object frame).
editor.place.bakeTitle: Off (default): the placement becomes the GLB root node transform. On: it is applied to the top-level nodes instead.
editor.match.master.setTitle: Make the selected {axis} line the master of its axis
editor.match.master.label: ★ Master {axis}
editor.match.master.cycleAria: Make the next {axis} line the master
editor.match.master.setToast: ★ Line {name} is now the master of axis {axis}
editor.match.master.promoted: Deleted the master of axis {axis} — line {name} (lowest residual) is the new master
editor.match.master.onlyMaster: Only the master so far — add another {axis} line
editor.match.master.legendText: : the reference line of its axis — the vanishing point lies on it (parallel: its direction); a converging axis may have two (★1 ★2): the VP is then exactly their intersection and the other lines only show residuals · Merge / Parallel / edge snapping never move a master · ★ toggles it here, or long-press / right-click a line
editor.match.master.toggleTitle: Toggle the selected {axis} line as a master (a converging axis can have two: the VP is their intersection)
editor.match.master.secondToast: ★2 Line {name} is the second master of axis {axis} — the vanishing point is now exactly where the two masters cross
editor.match.master.replacedOldestToast: Axis {axis} already had two masters — {old} (the oldest) is a normal line again; masters are now {m1} and {m2}
editor.match.master.parallelOne: Parallel axis {axis}: one master defines the direction — line {name} is now its only master
editor.match.master.parallelIgnored: Parallel axis: only ★1 sets the direction — ★2 ({name}) is ignored until the axis converges again
editor.match.master.unsetToast: Line {name} is no longer a master of axis {axis}
editor.match.master.keepOne: Axis {axis} needs a master — make another line the master first
editor.match.master.degenerate: Solve skipped: the vanishing points give a degenerate camera (nearly parallel masters?) — the camera is kept
editor.match.master.nearParallel: ⚠ The two masters of axis {axis} are nearly parallel ({deg}) — their crossing point (the VP) is unstable
editor.match.groups.roomHowTo: Trace walls, floor, ceiling, door/window frames
editor.match.groups.objectHowTo: Trace the edges of the object
editor.match.groups.roomSeedNote: Place room lines yourself along walls, floor, ceiling, door (the current camera does not know the room shape)
editor.match.snap.label: Line snap
editor.match.snap.title: Line snap (hold Alt = off temporarily)
editor.match.snap.unlinked: Unlinked the corners of the selected line
editor.match.snap.cornerSplit: Corner split — this line end now moves freely
editor.match.snap.cornerLinked: Corner linked — the ends move together (long-press the corner to split)
editor.match.snap.tipDrag: Drag a line end (or the whole line) near a line of another axis to snap to its end, intersection or segment · snapped ends become
editor.match.snap.tipHoldRest: a corner to split it · hold Alt while dragging to turn snapping off temporarily
editor.match.vp.heading: Consolidated vanishing points
editor.match.vp.headingNote: (best point from all lines of each axis)
editor.match.vp.consolidateTitle: Merge all lines into one vanishing point (auto mode)
editor.match.vp.parallelTitle: Make all lines parallel along their mean direction (vanishing point at ∞)
editor.match.vp.hintFar: vanishing point is {diag} image diagonals away
editor.match.vp.hint: 💡 Axis {axis} looks parallel — {why} · tap to use "Parallel {axis}"
editor.match.vp.lockToastOn: Lock to vanishing point: on (axes with 3+ lines)
editor.match.vp.legendColor: Line outline = angle off the vanishing point:
editor.match.vp.legendConsolidateText: rotates every line about its midpoint (or its linked corner) through one point
editor.match.vp.legendLockText: : a dragged line end keeps the line pointing at the vanishing point of the other lines
editor.match.vp.legendParallelText: : vanishing point at ∞ (e.g. the Z axis of a level camera, no pitch) — the camera is constrained so that axis is parallel to the image · two parallel axes (one-point perspective) need a locked lens or point pairs
editor.match.vp.needTwoBeforeParallel: Needs at least 2 lines{name} before making them parallel
editor.match.vp.needTwoBeforeConsolidate: Needs at least 2 lines{name} before merging vanishing points
editor.match.vp.madeParallel: Lines{name} made parallel · adjusted {n} lines to the mean direction (vanishing point at ∞)
editor.match.vp.consolidated: Merged vanishing point{name} · adjusted {n} lines to pass through one point
editor.match.vp.alreadyConsolidated: Lines{name} already pass through one vanishing point
editor.match.vp.skippedLinked: · skipped {n} lines (both ends linked — unlink first)
editor.match.vp.skipPivotAtVp: pivot is at the vanishing point
editor.match.vp.onePointNoLens: Two parallel axes (one-point perspective): the lens cannot be found from lines — lock the lens or use point pairs
editor.match.vp.oneRealVpNoLens: Only one finite vanishing point: the lens cannot be found from lines — add lines on another axis, lock the lens or use point pairs
editor.match.vp.principalNeedsThree: The principal point needs three finite vanishing points (an axis is parallel)
editor.match.detect.heading: Detect lines
editor.match.detect.runTitle: Find straight edges in this view and propose them as guide lines (also runs when image edges are set to Always)
editor.match.detect.found: {n} candidates (X {x} · Y {y} · Z {z} · no axis {u}) — click one to accept · 1/2/3 sets its axis · Esc clears
editor.match.detect.none: No straight edges found — try a shorter minimum length
editor.match.detect.needAxis: This candidate has no axis yet: hover it and press 1/2/3, or right-click it
editor.match.detect.legend: Dashed thin lines = detected candidates in the axis colour (grey = no axis yet). They are not saved until you accept them.
editor.match.axisOrigin.heading: Axis origin
editor.match.axisOrigin.headingNote: (where X, Y and Z meet in the image)
editor.match.axisOrigin.notSet: Not set — the model origin keeps its current pixel
editor.match.axisOrigin.fromOther: Using the {group} origin (none set on this view)
editor.match.axisOrigin.noCandidates: No corner where X, Y and Z lines meet yet — draw or accept lines through a corner
editor.match.axisOrigin.placeTitle: Origin mode: click a corner marker (or any point — it snaps to line crossings) or drag the ringed handle. Esc ends.
editor.match.axisOrigin.modeOn: Click a corner (or drag the ringed handle) to set the axis origin · Alt = no snap · Esc to finish
editor.match.axisOrigin.set: Axis origin set — the world origin now sits on that pixel
editor.match.axisOrigin.setNoCam: Axis origin stored; the camera will use it after the next line solve
editor.match.axisOrigin.flipTitle: Flip the {axis} direction (turns {other} with it so the axes stay right-handed)
editor.match.axisOrigin.objectNote: Object view: the model origin (its pivot with the default whole-object placement) sits on this corner. Move the object with G afterwards if needed.
editor.match.axisOrigin.roomNote: Room view: the world origin sits on this corner; the object keeps its placement relative to it.
editor.match.axisOrigin.legend: Small 3-colour corners = candidates (click to use). Drag the ringed handle to move the origin; it snaps to corners and line crossings, Alt = no snap. Tripod: X red, Y green, Z blue.
editor.match.edges.heading: Line vs image edges
editor.match.edges.headingNote: (guide line ↔ real edges in the mock-up)
editor.match.edges.noneNearLine: No image edge near the line
editor.match.edges.snapWhileDragToastOn: Snap to image edge while dragging: on (Alt = off temporarily)
editor.match.edges.snapWhileDragToastOff: Snap to image edge while dragging: off
editor.match.edges.legendLead: The image dims and detected edges glow · short ticks from line to edge = actual offset:
editor.match.edges.legendRefineText: fits the line to edges within ±8 px (linked corners stay put), undoable
editor.match.edges.noClearEdge: No clear image edge in the band around the line
editor.match.edges.selectFirst: Select a line first (tap it) or press “All lines”
editor.match.edges.refinedMany: Snapped {n} lines to image edges · mean offset {before} → {after} px
editor.match.edges.nothingToRefine: Lines are already on image edges, or no clear edge is near them
editor.match.diff.label: Difference view against the model (model ⊖ image: match = dark, mismatch = bright) · default off
editor.match.diff.solveFailed: Camera solve failed · using the last one
editor.match.room.aligned: Object aligned with the room (same X/Y axes as the walls)
editor.match.room.yawLead: Object rotated from the room by
editor.match.room.yawRest: (about Z) · only vertical/horizon/lens are shared · rotate the model {deg}° about Z when placing it in the room (in the export)
editor.match.room.drawBoth: Draw both object (crop) and room (full mock-up) lines to check that they agree
editor.match.room.highlighted: Highlighted the {n} worst lines of axis {axis}
editor.match.room.legendTap: Tap an axis to highlight its worst lines (both sets)
editor.match.room.needTwoInTwoAxes: Needs at least 2 lines in 2 axes
editor.match.room.needXYBoth: Needs X/Y lines in both object and room to find the yaw (keeping the previous one)
